references.text: The same principle of leaving the leftovers of the harvest for the poor, foreigners, fatherless, and widows also applies to vineyards.
Part of the same law section that deals with leaving the leftovers of the harvest for vulnerable groups in society - foreigners, fatherless, and widows.
Ruth, who was a foreigner and widow, was allowed to glean among the grain after the harvesters in accordance with this law.
Boaz instructs his workers to let Ruth glean among the sheaves of grain, as a practical application of the law about leaving leftovers for the poor.
A parallel law about leaving the corners of the field and gleaning for the poor and foreigners.
The same groups are mentioned - foreigner, fatherless, and widow - as recipients of God's care through the generosity of the Israelites.
